formal_verdict: passed: six independent exact full-forall contracts, 95 imported project theorem axiom audits, and 16 independent boundary consumers
scope: Finite nonempty index type; real finite logits; scalar softmax coordinate; global convexity and coordinatewise monotonicity of both heads on the full expanded space; nonnegativity restricted to the nonnegative expanded orthant.
formula: F_i^±(x,y) = [log(sum_j exp(x_j-y_j)) ± exp(x_i-y_i)/sum_j exp(x_j-y_j) + sum_j y_j]/2 - [log(d)-1/d]/2
independent_arguments: For a scalar logit line, p is a probability vector, mu=sum_j p_j v_j and V=sum_j p_j(v_j-mu)^2. The second derivative of log-sum-exp is V; that of softmax_i is p_i((v_i-mu)^2-V).
For any nonnegative weights w_j, with V=sum_j p_j w_j, one has p_i w_i<=V and 0<=p_i<=1. Consequently -V<=p_i(w_i-V)<=V. Thus log-sum-exp plus or minus softmax_i is convex on every line.

The plus profile's diagonal gradient is p_i-p_i^2/2 and its off-diagonal gradient is p_j(1-p_i)/2. The minus profile's diagonal gradient is p_i^2/2 and its off-diagonal gradient is p_j(1+p_i)/2. All are in [0,1/2]; the last upper bound uses p_i+p_j<=1 for distinct coordinates.
The expanded lift has x-coordinate derivatives equal to the profile derivatives and y-coordinate derivatives equal to 1/2 minus those derivatives. This proves coordinatewise monotonicity globally.
The common affine term cancels exactly. At the origin F_i^+=1/d and F_i^-=0, yielding nonnegativity on the expanded nonnegative orthant by monotonicity.
boundary_cases: The singleton case is nonvacuous: F^+(x,y)=x/2+1 and F^-(x,y)=x/2.
Negative expanded inputs are allowed for convexity, monotonicity and exactness; the theorem must not promise nonnegative outputs there.
An empty index type is excluded because the real-valued formula is not the intended probability softmax.
A fixed nonempty attention support can instantiate the index type. An entirely masked attention row requires a separately specified convention.
The theorem is a real-arithmetic identity and does not establish floating-point stability or practical efficiency.
